newsitem.title: USA: Federal Signal sees gain from unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Federal Signal sees gain from unit sale.

text.p: Federal Signal Corp said Monday it expects to realize in 1996 an after-tax gain of approximately $3 million or $0.06 a share from the sale of its Bassett Rotary Tool subsidiary to Greenfield Industries Inc.
Greenfield announced earlier Monday that it acquired Bassett for about $14 million.
Federal Signal said it will use proceeds from the Bassett sale to retire debt.
Bassett makes rotary carbide cutting tools for the metal working industry and has sales of about $10 million.

"Bassett is the one domestic business in Federal Signal that does not have a leading market share in its served niche and consequently was not a core strategic holding for Federal," Joseph Ross, chairman, said in a statement. "When the opportunity arose to sell Bassett at a fair price to a company like Greenfield Industries, which is more focused on rotary cutting tools, we felt it was in the best interests of Federal Signal and Bassett to make this move."

Federal Signal makes safety and signaling equipment, emergency fire appartus and related equipment, street sweeping and vacuum loader vehicles, custom on-premise signs, and consumable tools and components.
